gen-gf-tektur-gf-karla: Karla reads stocky and friendly, its middle band tall and its c wide open. Karla could take a modest size, since its sturdy lowercase carries fine without any enlarging, while Tektur keeps its wiry, outsized look.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-kedebideri: Approachable letters carry the body here, rounded and open. Kedebideri stretches its tall x-height across a paragraph with a friendly, unhurried feel, while Tektur's wire-thin strokes stay sharper and more expressive up top.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-khula: Tektur draws every stroke with no thick or thin at all. Its wiry, oversized lowercase earns its keep in big, short headings, while Khula settles below with a tall midsection and curves that hold their mouths open.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-krub: Tektur has no hairlines anywhere, just uniform, wiry strokes. Krub follows with a pronounced x-height and curves that lift off before the loop closes, so a long passage feels contemporary and unfussy.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-kufam: Contemporary and clean, Kufam draws one tube-like track width with generously open curves in the e. Tektur is best at expressive, oversized display lettering; Kufam does its best work in the body, where its big bodies dominate the line.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-lexend: Approachable and open, Lexend keeps every curve wide-jawed and its line thickness steady around the bends. Tektur does its best as an expressive, distinctive display voice, while Lexend is the plain sans that simply gets read.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-lexend-deca: Clean and approachable, Lexend Deca draws a plain line that never swells. Give it a modest size, since its big lowercase and small-looking capitals already feel generous, and leave Tektur's expressive heading to its own scale.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-liter: Wiry display letters meet a body with zero stroke contrast. Liter then carries a longer read comfortably, its lowercase standing tall and its round forms opening wide, a modern, professional texture against Tektur's showiness.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-mada: Tektur draws its letters like bent wire, expressive and distinctive, and that is what it does best in a heading. Mada does the quieter job below, with towering midzone letters and curves that refuse to close.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-martel-sans: Wire-thin and quirky on top, then a body with a high mean line. Martel Sans keeps its curves generously open under Tektur's uniform strokes, so the page moves from expressive to neutral without a jolt.
